messages.subject: RStan - avoid (re)compilation of the same mdoel
parts:
Hello,

I known this is not the group for Rstan, but I'm not sure where should I ask this.

If I distribute my software including Rstan model, I would like to avoid the compilation of the model because is the time consuming step. 2 questions:

1) is there a way to reading the compiled model, after the first compilation on a machine?
2) does the compiled model include data? (in this case obviously the program should be re-compiled every time)

For really quick runs (1-5 seconds), spending 15 seconds to compile is an excess.

Thanks,
Stefano

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] RStan - avoid (re)compilation of the same mdoel
parts:
> On Apr 22, 2016, at 11:36 PM, Stefano <mangiol...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> Hello,
>
> I known this is not the group for Rstan, but I'm not sure where should I ask this.

This is the only users list we have, so it's for everything.
We may split later based on modeling vs. interface issues, but
for now, everything's here.
> If I distribute my software including Rstan model, I would like to avoid the compilation of the model because is the time consuming step.

If you distribute as an R package, you can follow what RStanArm
does and include the compiled Stan program as part of the binary package.

> 2 questions:
>
> 1) is there a way to reading the compiled model, after the first compilation on a machine?

Yes, but I'm having trouble getting it to work reliably on
my Mac.
> 2) does the compiled model include data? (in this case obviously the program should be re-compiled every time)

No, new data doesn't require compilation, only a new Stan program.
That's why it's possible to include it with a package, and why
stan_model() is a separate function. (It should be called
something like stanc()
> For really quick runs (1-5 seconds), spending 15 seconds to compile is an excess.

Agreed. There's an option set_cppo(), but the doc only points to
a really long R doc, and then I found this:

http://rpackages.ianhowson.com/cran/rstan/man/set_cppo.html

The doc definitely needs to be fixed for this to either say
it doesn't do anything or say what it does. So now I don't know
how to control compiler optimization level.

- Bob
